passage:
Principal's note.

Jahnavi (Class 10) asked to see me on Tuesday, with her friend Rafiq beside her and her mother's permission. She was nervous but organised. She had dated notes: twice the maths teacher had refused to recheck her total and told her to stop questioning. She stuck to what happened and did not name motives. She told me she hadn't posted anything anywhere; she wanted the school to look at it first. Rafiq confirmed he had seen the second incident. I thanked them both and said I would go through the paper myself and speak to the teacher. I found an addition slip of several marks and have corrected it. I will meet the teacher about how students' queries are answered, and see Jahnavi again in a couple of weeks to ask if things feel different.

qa.q: Who came with Jahnavi to see the principal?
What did Jahnavi want by going to the school first instead of posting online?
qa.a: She wanted the school to look at it and fix it, so she trusted that the proper route would work.

qa.q: Why did Jahnavi's approach of dated notes and facts make it easier to solve?
qa.a: It gave the principal something clear to check. Sticking to what happened and not guessing motives let them find the addition slip and correct it.

qa.q: How does the principal seem to see Jahnavi's report?
qa.a: As a serious, responsible step. They thanked both students, checked the paper themselves and planned to meet the teacher and follow up with Jahnavi.

grounding: A student reports unfair treatment through the proper route, factually and with a friend, and gives it time.

passage:
For weeks, the sports teacher at the Bhimtal government school had been letting only boys use the new cricket kit. When Hafsa asked, he said, "Girls can play kho-kho."
Hafsa was furious. Her cousin said, "Post it online. Tag the education department. They'll be sorry."
She thought about it all night. Then she decided to go the proper way first. She wrote down four dates when the girls had been refused, and what was said.
On Monday, she and her friend Maria went to the principal's office with their class teacher. Hafsa read out the dates calmly. "We're not asking for special treatment. Just a fair turn."
The principal listened without interrupting. "Thank you for coming to me first, with facts. I'll speak to the sports teacher today and set a timetable for the kit by next week."
It took ten days, not one. But the timetable went up on the notice board, with the girls' team on Tuesdays and Fridays.

qa.q: What did the sports teacher tell Hafsa girls could play?
How did Hafsa feel when she was refused the cricket kit?
qa.a: She felt angry and treated unfairly, and was tempted to post about it online.

qa.q: Which choice did Hafsa make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She reported it through the principal with written dates, a friend and her class teacher, which gave the school a fair chance to fix it.

qa.q: How does the principal see Hafsa's complaint?
qa.a: The principal takes it seriously, appreciates her coming first with facts, and acts by setting a fair timetable.

grounding: A teen reports unfair treatment to the principal with facts and a friend, trusting the school to fix it rather than posting online first.

passage:
At his school in Gdańsk, Marek's geography teacher had given him zero for a project because, she said, it "looked too good to be his own." He had worked on it for three weeks, and he had the drafts to prove it.
He was furious. His classmate Astrid said, "Post the drafts online. Show everyone she's wrong."
Marek wanted to. But he thought about how that would look, and how it might make things worse. Instead, he gathered the drafts, the dated photos of his work, and asked Astrid to come with him.
On Thursday they sat in the principal's office. Marek explained calmly, pointing to each draft.
The principal, Mrs Nowak, listened carefully. "You were right to bring this to me first, with evidence. I'll ask the teacher to review the project with me this week."
The review took eight days. On the ninth, Marek's mark was changed to a B-plus, with a note: "Well researched."

qa.q: How long had Marek worked on the project?
How did Marek feel when he got a zero?
qa.a: He felt furious and wronged, tempted to post his drafts online to prove the teacher wrong.
He gathered evidence, brought Astrid, went to the principal calmly and gave the process time instead of posting online first.

qa.q: How does Mrs Nowak respond to Marek's complaint?
qa.a: She takes it seriously, praises him for coming first with evidence, and arranges a review with the teacher.

grounding: A teen reports unfair treatment to the principal with evidence and a friend, trusting the proper route instead of posting online.
